verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents an official MCP server (local and hosted) and a CLI for managing flags, plus scoped API access tokens, so the agent-access half of the story is well covered. The governance half is only partly evidenced: the approvals docs describe members having the 'option to request approval' for a change, not a policy that forces agent-originated API, CLI or MCP writes through review before they reach production. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that approvals can be required (not optional) for production changes, evidence that MCP/CLI/API writes are routed into approval workflows, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed
